column4: dialect-gated: single CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL gate (not a registeredBackends subtest), so it costs one skip rather than two. Measured: env -u CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL go test ./engine/ -run TestMSSQLDeleteExpiredEventsSurvivesMoreThan2100Workflows -count=1 -json | grep -c '"Action":"skip"' reports 1. Guards cleat#2103: SQL Server's 2100-parameter-per-statement cap crashed a retention sweep outright once more than ~2100 distinct workflows were swept in one pass. Runs in test-mssql, the only job with CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL set.

dialect-gated: single CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL gate, one skip. Isolates chunkedMarkHistorySwept's own chunking from mssqlEventRowChunk's margin, so it still catches cleat#2103's crash if mssqlEventRowChunk is ever raised past 2100 independently. Measured the same way as the line above: 1.

dialect-gated: single CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL gate, one skip (the three dialect arms are t.Run subtests inside one Skip-gated parent, not a registeredBackends test, so the parent's own Skip is what's counted). Guards cleat#2060: SQL Server escalates row/page locks to a table lock on event_history once one transaction holds roughly 5,000 locks on it, blocking every tenant's event writes until it finishes; the fix row-bounds and interleaves the delete so a single call never approaches that threshold. Measured: env -u CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL go test ./engine/ -run TestMSSQLRetentionSweepsCauseNoLockEscalation -count=1 -json | grep -c '"Action":"skip"' reports 1.
